Maggie: Bringing up orion-2b-lite on int4 tonight. Quick summary: small model but we're hitting OOMs when batch_size >= 6 with max_new_tokens 256.
Jay: Can you paste the OOM log?
Maggie: Sure:
```
ERROR: cuda out of memory. Alloc tried 1.2GB at kv_cache.cpp:142
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
RuntimeError: CUDA OOM when allocating buffer for KV cache
```
Nina: Is this with prefetch enabled? Prefetch + int4 can blow up due to padding.
Maggie: Yep prefetch=on, evict_window=30. With prefetch off batch_size 8 works but latency doubles.
Omar: Did we try int8 fallback? Quality seems worse in int4 on our summarization eval.
Maggie: Linked quick eval numbers: int4 rougeL 34.2, int8 35.8, fp16 36.0
Jay: That's a measurable reg. Maybe quantization params need calibration for this checkpoint.
Leo: Could also be fragmentation; int4 uses different allocator path. Any spikes in headroom between requests?
Maggie: Memory pressure graph: shows gradual fragmentation after sustained 200 concurrent sessions. I suspect KV cache trim policy isn't kicking in early enough.
perf-bot: [automated] perf-regression detected for orion-2b-lite: 8% increase in p95 latency after enabling prefetch
Nina: Proposed plan:
- turn off prefetch for canary (1 AZ) and run int4 onboard suite
- reduce default max_new_tokens from 256 -> 128 for hosted tier
- add aggressive kv_trim threshold at 0.75 headroom
- run quant-cal for int4 (20 calibration prompts)
Maggie: I can push a canary tomorrow 9am PT. Need someone to run the quant-cal job.
Omar: I'll take quant-cal. I'll also run compare eval: summarization + code-gen.
Jay: If int4 still lags after cal, fallback to int8 on hosted until we finish optimizer kernels.
Maggie: Sounds good. I'll open a tiny rollout PR with flags and add smoke tests.
Leo: Also add an alert: orion-2b-lite OOM rate > 0.5% -> rollback prefetch
Maggie: added to checklist. Thanks :thumbsup:
